confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from web searches of aggregated cost-of-living sources (Citycost, Whereandwhen, Travel Compass, combien-coute.net). These sources gave about CHF 24.6 for an inexpensive meal, CHF 116 for a mid-range three-course dinner for two, CHF 4-6 (about CHF 4.8) for a cappuccino and about CHF 7 for a 0.5 L draught beer. I converted CHF to USD at about 1.23-1.25 USD per CHF, based on the conversion shown in Citycost's own figures. These sources are partly crowdsourced and not clearly dated. I raised the estimates slightly to account for July peak-season tourist pricing. My searches did not find a reliable aggregated price for cocktails or wine by the glass in Interlaken. The cocktail (about CHF 18) and glass of wine (about CHF 9) are bounded estimates based on how they usually compare with beer prices in Switzerland, so they are less certain. All four accommodation anchors are my own estimates for July 2026 peak summer demand, made without looking at live booking pages or listings. They have the widest uncertainty, roughly ±25%.
comparable_city_reasoning: Interlaken is a small resort town that depends heavily on tourism. Its restaurant prices are close to Zurich and Bern levels (Citycost's Interlaken-vs-Zurich comparison shows almost the same budget meal price). Its summer accommodation prices are high, similar to other Bernese Oberland and Alpine resort towns such as Grindelwald and Lucerne in peak season.
